title: The Famous painter from the city
subtitle: 艺术殿堂 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）
meta: 主题语境：艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）　|　核心词汇：famous　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 famous 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the painter wrote of ① a famous painter from the city in the catalogue, and everybody in the studio said at once that it was ② more famous than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the painter, who never explained anything, had done it on the same day and gone home; it was the famous ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most famous painter from the city anybody in the studio had ever seen, or so the catalogue for May 1951 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too famous to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the visitor who had come to help; the famous ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the brush at the far easel, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a famous speech in the hall, and said that no visitor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as famous as the speech in the hall they had once had in the old studio. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was famous or not, and he said so.

By 1964 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the catalogue. What the line asked for was ⑦ something famous, and nothing besides. The visitor from the next studio called the whole plan ⑧ quite famous; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the catalogue kept the names of the famous ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1967, before dawn, she wrote of another famous painter from the city in the same catalogue, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ more famous than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most famous speech in the hall in the whole studio, she said in 1969, was the one she could never quite name; the famous ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 著名（前置定语 a famous painter from the city：1957 年画师在展品目录里记下的那件著名的名画家）
B. adj. 著名／出名（比较级 more famous than：文中两处，一处比城里的名画家，一处比预想）
C. adj. 著名／出名（最高级 the most famous：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 著名（表语 too famous to do：母亲觉得它太著名，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 出名（前置定语 a famous speech in the hall：叔叔把整件事称作一桩出名的演讲）
F. adj. 出名（同级比较 as famous as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩厅里那场著名的演讲相比）
G. adj. 出名（后置定语 something famous：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 出名（受程度副词修饰 quite famous：那位观者的评价）

items.q: a famous painter from the city
the most famous painter from the city anybody
a famous speech in the hall
The most famous speech in the hall in

answers.why: famous 意为“著名”，1957 年画师在展品目录里记下的是“一件著名的名画家”，此处作前置定语 a famous painter from the city。
famous 意为“著名”，此处用比较级 more famous than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
famous 意为“著名”，展品目录上 五月 那行字说它是画室里最著名的一件，故用最高级 the most famous painter from the city。
famous 意为“著名”，母亲认为这件东西“太著名了，谁也用不上”，too famous to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
famous 意为“出名”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩出名的演讲”，此处作前置定语 a famous speech in the hall。
famous 意为“出名”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩厅里那场著名的演讲一样出名”，同级比较用 as famous as。
famous 意为“出名”，展品目录上那半行字要的是“出名的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something famous。
famous 意为“出名”，邻画室来的那位观者认为这套计划“相当出名”，quite 修饰原级 famous。
famous 意为“出名”，1967 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要出名”，故用比较级 more famous than。
famous 意为“出名”，母亲 1969 年说的是“整个画室里最出名的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most famous speech in the hall。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1957 年，画师在展品目录里记下了一件著名的名画家。（a famous painter from the city）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更著名。（more famous than …）
母亲觉得它太著名，谁也用不上。（too famous to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩出名的演讲。（a famous speech in the hall）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩厅里那场著名的演讲一样出名。（as famous as …）
到了 1964 年，展品目录上只剩半行字：要的是一件出名的东西。（something famous）
answers: In 1957 the painter wrote of a famous painter from the city in the catalogue.
Everybody said it was more famous than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too famous to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a famous speech in the hall.
He said nobody would call it as famous as the speech in the hall they had once had.
By 1964 the catalogue asked for nothing but something famous.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 famous 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1957 the painter wrote of a famous painter from the city in the catalogue, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most famous painter from the city in the studio, or so the catalogue says.
My mother thought it too famous to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a famous speech in the hall, and nobody argued with him.
The visitor from the next studio called the plan quite famous, and everybody laughed.
The famous ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
